verses.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together. They went without food, wore rough sackcloth, and put dust on their heads.
Those who were descended from Israel separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood and confessed their own sins and the sins of their ancestors.

They stood in their places and listened for a quarter of the day while the book of the law of the LORD their God was read. For another quarter of the day they confessed their sins and worshiped the LORD their God.
The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the stairs and cried out loudly to the LORD their God.

Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and praise the LORD your God, who lives forever and ever! Praise your glorious name, LORD. It is greater than all our blessing and praise!

You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, and all the stars. You made the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You give life to everything, and the armies of heaven worship you.
You are the LORD God who chose Abram. You brought him out of Ur of the Babylonians and gave him the name Abraham.

You saw that his heart was faithful to you. You made a covenant with him to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites. You have kept your promise, because you are right and fair.
You saw how our ancestors suffered in Egypt. You heard them cry out at the Red Sea.

You did signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the people of his land, because you knew how proudly they treated our ancestors. You made a name for yourself that lasts to this day.
You split the sea in front of them, so they walked through the middle of it on dry ground. But you threw those chasing them into the deep water, like a stone into rough waters.
You led them with a pillar of cloud by day, and with a pillar of fire by night to light up the way they should go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them fair rules, true laws, and good orders and commands.
You taught them about your holy Sabbath. Through your servant Moses you gave them commands, rules, and laws.
When they were hungry, you gave them bread from heaven. When they were thirsty, you brought water out of a rock for them. You told them to go in and take the land you had promised to give them.
But our ancestors became proud and stubborn, and they did not obey your commands.

They refused to listen. They forgot the miracles you did among them. They became stubborn and, in their rebellion, chose a leader to take them back to slavery in Egypt. But you are a God who forgives. You are kind and merciful, slow to become angry, and full of faithful love. You did not leave them,
even when they made a metal statue of a calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt.' They spoke terrible insults against you,

but because of your great mercy you did not leave them in the desert. The pillar of cloud did not stop leading them on their way during the day, and the pillar of fire did not stop lighting the way for them at night.
You gave your good Spirit to teach them. You did not stop giving them manna to eat, and you gave them water when they were thirsty.
For forty years you took care of them in the desert, and they had everything they needed. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
You gave them kingdoms and nations, and you gave them land in every direction. They took over the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You made their children as many as the stars in the sky. You brought them into the land you had told their ancestors to go in and take.

So their children went in and took the land. You defeated the Canaanites who lived in the land ahead of them. You handed them over to them, with their kings and the peoples of the land, so they could do what they wanted with them.

They captured walled cities and fertile land. They took over houses full of good things, wells already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and lots of fruit trees. They ate until they were full and grew fat. They enjoyed your great goodness.
But they disobeyed you and rebelled against you. They turned their backs on your law. They killed your prophets, who had warned them to come back to you. They spoke terrible insults against you.

So you handed them over to their enemies, who made them suffer. But when they were in trouble, they cried out to you, and you heard them from heaven. Because of your great mercy, you gave them rescuers who saved them from their enemies.

But as soon as they had peace, they did evil again in front of you. So you left them to their enemies, who ruled over them. When they cried out to you again, you heard them from heaven. Again and again you rescued them because of your mercy.

You warned them to come back to your law, but they were proud and did not obey your commands. They sinned against your rules, the rules that give life to anyone who obeys them. They stubbornly turned their backs on you and would not listen.
For many years you were patient with them. Your Spirit warned them through your prophets, but they would not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of other lands.
But because of your great mercy, you did not destroy them completely or leave them. You are a kind and merciful God.

Now, our God, you are the great, powerful, and amazing God. You keep your covenant of faithful love. Do not think lightly of all the hardship that has come on us, on our kings, leaders, priests, prophets, ancestors, and all your people, from the time of the kings of Assyria until today.
You have been fair in everything that has happened to us. You have been faithful, but we have done wrong.
Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors did not obey your law. They did not listen to your commands or the warnings you gave them.
Even while they had their own kingdom, enjoying all the good things you gave them in the large, fertile land you gave them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil ways.
Look, today we are slaves. We are slaves in the land you gave our ancestors so they could enjoy its fruit and its good things.
Its great harvest goes to the kings you have put over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our animals as they please. We are in great trouble.
Because of all this, we are making a firm agreement and writing it down. Our leaders, our Levites, and our priests are putting their seals on it."
